answer: The BLIS 6-knob configuration space has a Pareto front concentrated in a low-GPU, high-TP, moderate-KV subspace. Tensor parallelism (tp) and topology selection are the dominant knobs: tp=4,inst=1 (4 GPUs, 19.56 rps) outperforms tp=1,inst=8 (8 GPUs, 11.93 rps). KV cache capacity has a saturating dose-response — below a model-dependent threshold (~120k effective tokens for qwen3-14b), preemptions cause severe TTFT spikes; above it, performance plateaus with byte-identical results. Secondary knobs (scheduler, max_num_running_reqs, block_size_in_tokens) provide refinements but rarely change the Pareto front structure. A 4-phase adaptive search algorithm (ceiling+cheapest scan, boundary mapping, sensitivity testing, strategic fill) achieves 100% Pareto coverage within ~100 evaluations (well within the 200-eval budget), with a sharply saturating budget-coverage curve (57.7% at 50 evals, 100% at 100 evals). The algorithm generalizes across dense models (7B-70B), MoE models (Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E), arrival rates (50-200 req/s), and random seeds — 100% coverage in all 12 model x rate x seed combinations tested.
